correctness.rationale: A separated unordered pair at distance d gains (1-p)p^(d-1) after its path edge is upgraded. Doubling and dividing by n gives the stated increment for uniform starting patch, with no gain for diagonal pairs. PC and ECA are monotone transforms here. I generated all shapes by leaf extension from the singleton, not by replaying the packaged Prüfer verifier: deleting a leaf shows inductive exhaustiveness, and minimizing sorted rooted codes over all roots identifies exactly the unrooted isomorphism classes. I rebuilt the polynomials from unique endpoint paths. The counts for n=2..8 are 1,1,2,3,6,11,23. After deleting strictly coefficientwise dominated vectors there is one two-vector frontier at n=7, with difference p(1-p), and four at n=8, with differences up to sign p(2-p), p(1-p²), p(2p-1), and p(p²+p-1). The first two never change sign in the open interval; the other two are the stated witnesses and each crosses once. All noncandidate edges in the witnesses have a coefficientwise dominating candidate with at least one strict coefficient; the equal vectors identify the stated tied edges. This is a continuum certificate, not a probability grid.

value.rationale: The first obstruction to parameter-independent edge intervention is a natural extremal invariant. The complete frontier classification rules out smaller obstructions and explains both eight-vertex switch mechanisms and ties, rather than reporting selected evaluations or arbitrary small counts. Its use is as a tree reliability benchmark, not ecological field guidance.
